title: 17th Sitting of second session of 2025
summary: After routine business (minutes accepted, committee deadlines for three bills announced), members debated a resolution from the North Galolhu member asking the Majlis to state its view on the long-delayed K-Park Residence flats in Hulhumale', where buyers paid deposits but have not received flats. Speakers from several parties agreed the buyers are in difficulty but disagreed about which past government or the housing corporation (HDC) carries responsibility, with two points of order and repeated chair reminders not to make remarks that harm other members' reputations. No vote on the resolution is recorded in this part; the sitting recessed, and afterwards the Human Rights and Gender Committee presented its report recommending a five-year extension of the Children's Ombudsperson's term, with debate on it just beginning when this part ends. The text is heavily garbled in places, so speech gists are approximate. This part picks up mid-debate on the Human Rights and Gender Committee's report recommending a five-year extension of the Children's Ombudsperson's term. One member whose opening header is in part 1 argued that someone should stay in the role to support families and children, and the Vaikaradhoo member then spoke, saying an open announcement and election would have been ideal but he accepted an extension given the two new child-rights laws. The chair closed debate, and in the vote the extension passed with 50 yes, none against and none abstaining (52 present, 26 needed). The sitting then ended, with the next sitting set for 22 July 2025 at 9:00; the text is partly garbled so speech gists are approximate.

speakers.name: Mohamed Abbas
positions: Said the resolution is welcome but debate should focus on solutions, and that the previous government's 4,000 flats were never handed over to buyers.
Argued the current government has failed on housing and cost of living, citing prices, inflation, the dollar rate and delayed island projects.
Objected to interruptions during his speech and asked the chair to protect members' freedom to debate.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Falah
positions: Said the issue is serious, traced it to 2017-18, and argued the MDP government had five years in which to resolve it.
Questioned the sincerity of the resolution, noted it was allowed to be debated by the PNC majority, and said the government will work on a solution.
Raised a point of order that remarks by the Velidhoo member targeted his reputation; the chair advised members to avoid such remarks.

speakers.name: Hussain Shareef
positions: Argued that a 7,000-flat allocation under the 2013-18 government was scrapped and re-allocated after 2018, and linked K-Park buyers' difficulties to MDP-era decisions.
Said the current government is restarting stalled housing projects through HDC.
Raised a point of order objecting to the Velidhoo member's remarks on a Foddhoo project; the chair asked members to keep to facts.

speakers.name: Hussain Ziyad
positions: Supported speeding up a solution to the buyers' delays and noted the case is now before the courts.
Said housing disputes such as police, army and Sea Life flats went unresolved under earlier governments, and recalled the current President was Housing Minister for about two and a half years.
Said the Majlis housing committee should take up the matter and hoped the current Housing Minister would help speed up a resolution.
Said the best course would have been to announce the vacancy and hold an election before the term ended, rather than a decree-style appointment.

speakers.name: Mohamed Ibrahim
positions: Introduced the resolution: buyers paid down payments for K-Park Residence flats in Hulhumale' but the project stayed unfinished for years.
Said buyers face financial loss and were blocked from applying to government social housing schemes; asked the Majlis for its view.

speakers.name: Mohamed Nazim
positions: Said many constituents are affected, paying bank loans and rent, and that earlier governments did not solve it; he believes this government can.
Said courts and police processes have not delivered results for buyers; urged referring the matter to a committee.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Hussain
positions: Argued HDC bears major responsibility and that the previous MDP government did not resolve the K-Park or Sea World cases.
Noted the Finance Committee and the SOE Committee are already looking into the K-Park matter.

speakers.name: Abdul Gafoor Moosa
positions: Said such disputes arise under any government when agreements with companies are not followed, and that HDC carries a large share of responsibility.
Argued buyers' payments should be held in dedicated accounts released as construction progresses, and agreements should protect buyers and the state.

speakers.name: Mauroof Zakir
positions: Opened by expressing concern over attacks on Palestinians and urging Maldives to do all it can.
Said hundreds of buyers have been denied justice and a government's duty is a lasting solution; cited the Constitution's guarantees.
Criticised rising prices, the dollar shortage and spending on an airport terminal ceremony; urged calling the MMA governor to the Majlis.

speakers.name: Meekail Ahmed Nasym
positions: Said the government's priorities are misplaced, citing reclamation of Fushidhiggaru while K-Park buyers and basic housing wait.
Said buyers pay bank loans and rent while waiting; asked why handover has been delayed for years.

speakers.name: Abdul Latheef Mohamed
positions: Said the K-Park and Sea Life problems began under the MDP government and that this government is working in good faith to solve them.
Said the government will act within law and needs time, and criticised the opposition for repeatedly tabling motions.

speakers.name: Saudulla Hilmy
positions: Expressed concern for affected buyers; said HDC bears responsibility but has made changes, such as payments tied to construction progress.
Said those who take public money through corruption should be investigated and the money recovered.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Nazil
positions: Said K-Park was awarded in 2016 with completion due in 2018, and that a criminal case over payments was filed during the MDP government.
Said civil servants told the 2018 transitional committee that flats had been allocated to selected families within about 24 hours.
Urged members and businesspeople to go to the MMA together over the dollar shortage.

speakers.name: Ibrahim Didi
positions: Called the K-Park matter a major theft and said refunds and accountability should come through the courts.
Thanked the sponsor, saying the PNC majority allowed the debate, and said the previous government did not act in its five years.
Argued the dollar rate and national debt rose under the previous government and defended the current government's development record.

speakers.name: Ahmed Azaan Marzooq
positions: Said the first priority is relief for buyers who took bank loans, such as pausing repayments, and securing housing for them through other schemes.
Argued the long-term fix is legal reform: real estate laws, escrow-style accounts, project insurance and faster dispute resolution.
Supported the government identifying affected parties and finding a solution.

speakers.name: Ameen Faisal
positions: Said the problem is not tied to one government and any government that takes over inherits responsibility for resolving it.
Said affected buyers petitioned the President's Office in April 2024 and June 2025 without a reply; urged affected parties, including police and MNDF flat buyers, to seek compensation in court.

speakers.name: Fathimath Sauda
positions: Presented the Human Rights and Gender Committee report on the President's request to extend Children's Ombudsperson Nimaath Shafeeq's term.
Said the committee interviewed her and she averaged 88% against the usual 75% mark; the committee recommended a five-year extension.

decisions: Speaker declared the minutes of sittings 2025/2/12 to 2025/2/14 accepted, as no member had proposed amendments.
Speaker announced committee deadlines: Intellectual Property Office and Trademark bills (10 Aug 2025) and the public opinion referendum bill (11 Aug 2025).
Resolution on the K-Park Residence housing dispute introduced; preliminary debate opened with about 4 hours allotted across party groups, not concluded in this part.
Sitting recessed from 10:31 to 11:03 before committee items.
Human Rights and Gender Committee report recommending a five-year extension of the Children's Ombudsperson's term presented to the Majlis; no vote in this part.
The People's Majlis approved extending the term of the Children's Ombudsperson, Alfazila Nimaatha Shafeeg, by five years under Article 117 of Law 19/2019.
The next sitting was set for Tuesday 22 July 2025 at 9:00.

votes.what: Extend the Children's Ombudsperson's term by five years (Law 19/2019, Article 117)
